paragraphs.text: Keeps archived sessions out of the DSH conversation list and adds a panel to restore them or delete
them permanently - session log, archive and pin records, and projection cache.
# dsh-archive-purge
Keeps archived sessions out of the DSH conversation list, and gives them one place to be restored —
or **deleted for good**, which DSH itself deliberately has no path for.

> Looking for the npm name `dsh-archive-manager`? That one belongs to a different, unrelated
> plugi
n. This is `dsh-archive-purge`.
*Every screenshot here is rendered from invented sessions — no real titles, paths or sizes.*
## The two gaps it closes
DSH can archive a session, but:
- **Archiving is only a view concern.** The sidebar keeps rendering archived rows whenever *View opt
ions → Archived* is set to show them, and it keeps them in archived search results too. There is no

switch that means "never show these".
- **Nothing ever deletes a session.** `dsh-client-ui-workspace
` documents no session deletion and `dsh-session-persistence` documents no delete seam, so archived
sessions accumulate on disk forever.
This plugin closes both: it pins archived sessions out of the list, and it owns the erase path.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use your own profile name in place of `desktop` (for example `web`). Then switch it on under **Setti
ngs → Plugins**, where it appears as `dsh-archive-purge`. Turning it off disables the host routes an
d the browser panel together and leaves session data untouched.
## What it does
| | Behaviour |
| **Always hidden** | In the sidebar conversation list, an archived session row is never shown — wha
tever *View options → Archived* is set to. A component registered on `shell.overlay` writes `[data-r
ow-key="session:<id>"]{display:none}` for every id in the registry's `archivedSessionIds`, plus a fa
llback rule keyed on the accessible description so archived search-result rows are covered as well.

|
| **Filter reset** | The browser-persisted `dsh.workspace.view.v5` has its `archivedFilter` reset
to the shipped default (`default`, i.e. "hide archived"), so the menu stops claiming "All conversati

ons (show archived)" while showing nothing. |
| **Management panel** | A sidebar icon plus a centre-
column panel lists every archived session with its workspace, path, disk footprint, creation time an

d child-session count; it supports search, multi-select and batch unarchive. |
| **Permanent delete*
* | Delete sessions one at a time or in bulk, behind a confirmation dialog that names the sessions,
their size, and exactly what will be removed. |
The panel takes its colours from the host's `--dsw-alias-*` tokens and ships English and Chinese wor
ding, so it follows whichever theme and locale the app is in rather than a look of its own.
## Permanent delete: the exact boundary
One delete removes four things:
1. **The session log directory** `<DSH_HOME>/sessions/<project>/<encoded-session-id>/` — the session

's own directory, every format generation in it, and any session-local artifact;
2. **The projection

-cache record** `<DSH_HOME>/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json`;
3. **The archive and pin

records** (`archivedSessionIds` / `pinnedSessionIds` in the workspace registry);
4. **The row in yo
ur browser** — announced through the session controller's own `api-session/removed` remote event (`@
mode emit`) so the client drops the row instead of leaving a clickable ghost.
**Deliberately kept:** attachment files. Attachments are content-addressed and may be shared with ot
her sessions, so they are out of scope. The panel says so at the bottom. An archived entry whose log
is already gone from disk only has its record cleaned up, and the button reads "Clear record" inste
already gone from disk only has its record cleaned up, and the button reads "Clear record" instead.
## Refusals run before any write
A batch reports each outcome separately: what was deleted and how much it freed, what had no log lef
t to delete, and what was refused — named, with the reason.
- The session is **not in the archive set** → skipped. Deletion is only ever available for archived

sessions.
- An **agent for that session still exists in this process** (`ctx.agents.get(id)`) → refu
sed (`live`). An agent may already hold the log's write handle, and deleting the file underneath it

would let the writer resurrect the log.
- The `workspace/session-activity` waterfall still reports *

*work in progress** → refused (`active`).
- The target directory is not **inside the configured sess
ions root**, or its name is not exactly the encoded session id → refused (`outside-root`).
Being merely *loaded* is deliberately **not** a refusal reason: the browser keeps an in-memory mirro
r for every rendered session row and never releases it, so refusing on that would make every archive
d session undeletable after enough browsing. The gate matches DSH's own archive gate (the activity w
aterfall) plus one cheaper agent check. Skipped and failed sessions are listed individually in the p
anel, with the reason.
## Ghost rows, and the two layers that remove them
DSH's browser session list is **event-driven**: it only adds and removes entries in response to `api
-session/added` / `api-session/removed`. A deleted session also leaves the archive set, so in the si
debar it goes from "hidden" to "should be shown" — and the cached row becomes a visible, clickable r
ow that fails with `session/not-found` when opened.
Two layers remove it:
- **Host side (authoritative).** After a successful delete and *before* the archive set is rewritten
, the host emits `ctx.emit('api-session/removed', id)` — the remote event the session controller def
ines and forwards for exactly this fact. The client receives a `{ kind: 'remove', sessionId }` chang
e and drops the row. Emitting before the registry write avoids a flash where the row is un-hidden an

d then disappears.
- **Client side (self-healing fallback).** The inventory carries `persistedIds` —
the session ids the host's persistence layer actually knows. The panel diffs the browser's cached i
ds against it, folds the remainder into the same hide rule, and shows the count under the title. The
diff is recomputed on every read rather than accumulated, so one failed read cannot permanently hid
e a live session. Ids deleted within this page session are tracked separately as a union, since that
needs no read to take effect.
